contexts.text: I will give thee () = that all things... are His. To give, in the sense of the letter, means that God should give to Him; as also... that the Father gave Him all things...; but in the internal sense... it means that the Lord acquired them...
Of the giver and the receiver, as of the agent and the patient, a like state is perceived.
Which God gave to Abraham () = which is from the Divine... God gave = appropriated to Him... for that which is given, is his to whom it is given.
To thee will I give it () = from proprium. AC 3705:3, Explained, Illustrated.
When He said that the Father gave to Him it meant that He Himself gave to Himself, and thus that it was from proprium.

All that Thou shalt give me, I will in tithing tithe it to Thee () = that He made each and all things Divine from His Own Divine power; (for) to give, when predicated of the Lord, = that He gave to Himself, thus that it was from His Own power.
For the Lord wills to give Himself, and what is His, to everyone; and He actually does give so far as they receive...
The word (from which Levi was named) means to mutually give and receive; moreover, by to mutually give and receive ... was represented mutual love...
Thou shalt not give me anything ()... = not to be brought from the good represented by Laban, but from the good represented by Jacob.
What ye say to me, I will give () = ... that on his part there was a mind, if there was a like mind on their part... for to give what they say = to make one with them as to truth and good. AC 4456.
To thee will I give it () = ... to appropriate to the Natural.
What dost thou give me that thou mayest come to me? () = what is reciprocal of conjunction, with a condition.
He gave into his hand () = ... into his Power.
He gave him into the house of the prison () = ... to be let into temptations as to... AC 5037.
(Not useful) that he should give to monasteries, nor even to wealthy places of worship.
Give us bread () = [supplication] concerning the support of spiritual life; (for) to give, when predicated of bread, = to support.
Give seed () = an influx of the good of charity and the truth of faith... That to give them = influx, is evident, because they come into man through influx from the Lord.

An Angel... wants to give everything to another, and to retain nothing... and then good flows... to him much more than he gives... From this it is evident that the Lord is in each of them; for the Lord is such that He wants to give Himself to all. DMin 4681.
To give to wife () = to adjoin. AC 8981.
The king of Egypt will not give you to go () = that falsity would set itself in opposition.
No chaff is given to thy servants () = that scientifics containant of truth are no longer furnished. AC 7152.
I have given thee a god to Pharaoh ().
Thou shalt give into our hand... () = that they should relinquish.
He will not give to the destroyer... () = that falsity and evil shall not approach.
Which He sware to the fathers to give thee () = which were promised from the Divine to those who are in good and truth... To swear to give = a promise.
Who will give... () = that it would have been better.
The goods of faith and charity cannot be given to man or Angel so as to be his Own... The reason life appears as their Own, is that the Lord... wills to give and conjoin all His own things to man...
Which Jehovah thy God giveth thee () = where there is the Divine, and thus influx... To give = influx; for Heaven with all... is the reception of influx from the Divine.
Thou shalt give soul for soul () = ... as thou hast done to another, so will it be done to thee. Explained.
To give to all who ask () = to confess all things of his own faith in the Lord.

For if a person were to give to everyone that asked... he would be deprived of all his goods; but... to give and to receive a loan means the communication of heavenly goods, which are those of the Knowledges of good and truth. For the case with this communication is, that the more an Angel, from the affection of charity, gives to another, the more flows in with him from the general good from Heaven, that is, from the Lord; so that by giving to him that asketh, an Angel is not deprived, but is enriched with goods.
The first-born of thy sons shalt thou give unto Me () = that all things of faith... are to be ascribed to the Lord, and not to self... To give to Me = to ascribe to the Lord. AC 10226.
To give into the hand () = to conquer and command.
Under Gift, see this reference.

The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, from the half of a shekel, to give to Jehovah () = that all, of every capacity whatever, ought alike to ascribe to the Lord all things of truth from good.

Thou shalt give it for the work of the Tent of the Assembly () = conjunction with Heaven through the acknowledgement that all truths and goods are from the Lord... (For) to give half a shekel = the ascription to the Lord of all things of love and faith.
To give wisdom in the heart () = to do these things from the Lord, thus from the good of love... AC 10336:4.
Man has no need to give his things to the poor, except in so far as affection leads him. SE 5794.
The faculty continually given by the Lord... DP 96:3.
Nothing exists or can exist, which is not from Him.
The Lord gives man to know... and He also gives to think the means.
This is meant by the good measure... which shall be given into the bosom of those who forgive and give to others (); that is, who are in the good of charity.
It was given to him to give spirit to the image of the beast... ()... By given is signified that it was permitted.

I will give to him that thirsteth... gratis () = that to those who long for truths for the sake of any spiritual use, the Lord will give from Himself through the Word all things which conduce to that use... To give gratis = from the Lord, and not from any self-intelligence of man.
In publicum dabitur.
They believe that it is charity to give to any poor person...
This is like giving bread to a devil, which he turns into poison.
See Czar.
He gave them to tell () = revelation.
Give to everyone that asketh thee = that it should be permitted.
Give me the little book (). (This implies action and reaction, or reciprocality.)
As charity towards the neighbour is meant, it is said... Give, and it shall be given unto you.
The fig and the vine shall give their force () = the production of the effect from...
I will give this city as Tophet ().
I will say to the north. Give ().
He shall give His voice ().
To give glory to Him () = to live according to the Divine truth. AE 986.
Not possible.
To give into their hearts () = to inspire affection.
To give their kingdom to the beast () = to give the Church to the Word...
To give glory () = to acknowledge, confess, and worship the Lord.
